text:
"Kennel cleaning, minutes at closing"
The agenda began with it
Attendees were Sana Schneider, Priya Garcia, and Maisie.

The group reviewed routine desk handling for passengers traveling with companion animals across Aurelia Skyways routes between skyports. Staff noted that the warm professional tone at the counter continues to steady anxious callers and walk-up guests, especially when a traveler is unsure about kennel fit, documents, or cabin placement. The senior coordinator reminded the team that clear, calm explanations prevent delays and reduce repeat questions. The record also noted that supervisors should continue to listen closely when a passenger is worried, then confirm the next step in plain language.

Attention then turned to kennel cleaning and end-of-shift checks. The team agreed that clean crates, secure latches, and dry liners are central to safe companion travel. Discussion covered the need to inspect surfaces for odor, fur, and loose fasteners before any kennel is returned to storage. Maisie was mentioned as a useful reminder that small passengers depend on a tidy setup and a steady hand. The staff also restated that found items must be labeled at once and routed through the usual storage shelf so the next traveler receives a ready kennel without delay.

A short service review followed. The desk noted steady demand for help with pet comfort, gate handoff, and seating coordination near the animal area. Staff agreed that the strongest results come when each case is handled with patience and consistent wording, since travelers respond well to the same dependable message at every contact point. The senior coordinator asked that brief notes be kept on any unusual behavior from animals in transit, since these notes support future planning and reinforce the company aim of dependable companion travel.

The meeting closed with a quick review of open follow-up items and a reminder to keep the counter orderly. No further business was raised, and the meeting ended.
